note: The workflow film for everyone on the board (16 October 2026: "where is the revised video to post that will guide all on the revised process, workflow etc so all will understand and take the test"). One client, start to finish: the letter, the call, the household named, the conversation, the log, the Salesforce task, the TT$200, the outcomes, and the test. Every name and number on screen is made up. build-boardfilm.py renders the film's page from this file; voice-lines.py voices the lines and times the scenes.

scenes.eyebrow: For agents, Client Support and managers
scenes.headline: From the letter to the TT$200
scenes.sub: One client, start to finish: what happens, who does it, and what counts
scenes.line: This is the client transition, start to finish, for everyone on the board. From the letter, to the agent, to the two hundred dollars.

scenes.headline: The notice, the facts, one tap
scenes.line: It starts with the letter. Guardian Life's notice. The facts off the client's own record. And answers they give with one tap. It goes from the branch's support address.

scenes.headline: Every client reached
scenes.line: Some clients answer the letter. The rest, Client Support calls, in order, with why to call and the number to tap. They take the details. They never advise.

scenes.eyebrow: On every call, whoever makes it
scenes.headline: Three rules on every call

rows.b: Nothing about the former agent beyond the notice
rows.i: never why, never where they went, never an opinion

rows.b: The former agent in touch? The branch calls first
rows.i: thank them, and do not ask what was said

rows.b: Nothing signed or paid until they have spoken to us

scenes.line: Three rules on every call. Nothing about the former agent beyond the notice. If the former agent has been in touch, a person from the branch calls first. And nothing is signed or paid until the client has spoken to us.

scenes.headline: The family stays together
scenes.line: Then the household is named, never one policy at a time. Each household carries one suggested agent. One press names the whole family. A manager can name a whole batch at once.

scenes.headline: Two records, one family?
scenes.line: Some families the records missed. The same surname, the same house, spelt two ways. The board shows the two side by side, with the family's cover and its gaps. One press makes them one household.

scenes.headline: One press, three things

rows.b: The agent gets a brief by e-mail
rows.i: every client named to them, with what each one told us

rows.b: Salesforce gets the agent, the date and the campaign
rows.i: on each of the client's policies

rows.b: A line goes on the client's open task
rows.i: named to the agent, on the day, by whoever pressed

scenes.line: That one press does three things. The agent gets a brief by e-mail. Salesforce gets the agent, the date and the campaign. And a line goes on the client's open task.

scenes.headline: Two working days. Read the file first.
scenes.line: The agent calls within two working days, and reads the file first. Their numbers, where they live, their family, what they told us, and why we are calling.

scenes.headline: Our service record
scenes.line: Every card carries our service record with the client. Every request we handled, how fast we closed it, and what kind of work it was.

scenes.headline: Log it the same day
scenes.line: Every try and every outcome goes on the board the same day. Press Log call. Choose what happened: called, met, no answer, declined or closed. Write one line for the file, and save.

scenes.headline: A note before every close
scenes.line: It posts to the client's Salesforce task, where every step goes on the Chatter. A no answer is a try, not a close. A task closes only with a note: who was spoken to, and what was agreed. If the client asked for an agent, it stays open until one is named. And the standard e-mail is never the close for a client who asked for something.

scenes.headline: The TT$200, by itself
scenes.line: When a service questionnaire comes in after the naming, the agent earns two hundred dollars. Nobody presses anything. The claim goes to the Retention unit at once. Every working day at ten, the unpaid claims go again, until the payment date is entered. Then the agent is told.

scenes.headline: The bar moves
scenes.line: Everything you log, the branch sees on the Agents tab. The bar moves, and the red flag clears. The Team tab shows who signs in, and the points each person earns.

scenes.headline: Seven outcomes

items.i: as a family, never one policy
the same day, board and Salesforce
in force, and reviewed every six months

scenes.line: Seven outcomes. Every household named. A first conversation in two working days. Every call logged the same day. Met or closed, with what was agreed. A review filed. The two hundred paid. And the policy kept.

scenes.headline: Read it. Take the test.
scenes.line: Before you start, open the training page. Sign in with the same number and password as the board. Read the workflow for your role, and tick each section. Then take the test. Your result goes to you, and to the branch manager.

scenes.headline: Read your workflow. Take your test. Open the board.
scenes.line: Read your workflow. Take your test. Then open the board.
